events.title: A spacecraft visits Pluto
events.description: New Horizons makes a close flyby after a journey of billions of miles.

events.title: UK voters choose to leave the EU
events.description: The referendum result begins a long process of leaving the European Union.

events.title: A total eclipse crosses the US
events.description: People along a narrow path see the Moon completely cover the Sun.

what_happened_next.text:
Apple gained about 220% and Tesla about 191% over five years. Hasbro also more than doubled, gaining about 123%. The U.S. share basket rose strongly, while the bond estimate ended slightly lower. Even several successful choices had different paths.

Hasbro’s game sales grew 8% in 2017, helping its total yearly sales rise 4%. Tesla built 34,494 vehicles in the first quarter of 2018 as it tried to increase Model 3 production. Apple reported its best March quarter then, with revenue growing across iPhone, Services and Wearables. These results show that toy games, electric cars and digital devices can each find buyers, but production capacity and competition still matter.

New Horizons passed Pluto in 2015. UK voters chose to leave the European Union in 2016, and a total solar eclipse crossed the United States in 2017. Those events mark the passing years without assigning a particular stock move to them. The small bond loss is also worth understanding: a bond is a loan, but a bond investment can still change in market value. Individual shares can do very well, but they differ from one another and from a basket.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: People discussed government decisions, immigration, books, music and how toys were marketed. The Fed described conditions for changing its support.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The amount of risk differed between shares and bonds, and between individual companies. Bonds could still lose value; they were not the same as cash.
reflection.what_faded_away: A first profitable quarter or a popular book was one moment in a longer story. Neither supplied a reliable five-year investment ranking.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The eventual gains and setbacks were unknown. Picking a strong business and paying a good price for its shares were separate questions.

hot:2013-05:hasbro.text: Hasbro’s game sales, including Monopoly and Magic: The Gathering, grew 8% to $1.50 billion in 2017. Total company sales rose 4% to $5.21 billion. Games helped the business grow even as sales of some toys based on partner brands, including Star Wars, fell.

hot:2013-05:tesla.text: In April 2018, Tesla said it built 34,494 vehicles in the first quarter, 40% more than in the previous quarter. It made 9,766 Model 3 cars as it tried to increase production. Building enough cars was a major challenge: orders mattered only if Tesla could manufacture and deliver the vehicles.

hot:2013-05:apple.text: Apple’s sales for the quarter ending in March 2018 reached $61.1 billion, its best March quarter yet. It reported growth in iPhone sales, services and wearable devices. More than one product line was bringing in extra money as Apple expanded beyond its original computer business.
